reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the original cap is per-Statement-of-Work 'fees paid' (potentially far below 12 months' fees of the engagement) and the sole carve-out cross-references Paragraph 9, the Independent Contractor clause, so none of the fallback's minimum carve-outs (indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct) exist. The clause therefore fails the fallback on material terms.

Redline is actionable and directionally right for the customer: it sets Contractor's cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, replaces the broken Paragraph 9 cross-reference with a defined mutual set of uncapped Excluded Claims tracking the model language, and confirms Company's fee payment obligation is not capped damages. The Company-side fees-paid cap amount (favourable to us) is preserved rather than raised.

Edit stays within the existing sentences of Section 7(a); the failed changed-character-ratio check on the second sentence reflects the rule-mandated insertion of the carve-out and payment-obligations language rather than an unnecessary rewrite. Section 7(b)'s mutual consequential-damages exclusion is correctly left alone.

Comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice: it states the position, explains the broken cross-reference, discloses that Excluded Claims now apply to both parties, and offers the straight 12-month fee cap fallback.

Minor, non-fatal: the rationale says the Company-side provision was 'left untouched', whereas the redline does extend the Excluded Claims carve-out to Company's cap (consistent with the playbook's mutuality requirement and disclosed in the comment); the 'indemnification obligations' carve-out is also a placeholder given no indemnity exists in the document.
